_readme: Launch Week data: real launches only (the placeholders are in data/launches.samples.json). The steps from a maker's assets to a
live launch are in README.md (Launch Week: from assets to a live launch). In short:
npm run launch:draft -- --email <file> | --submission <file>   draft an entry from a maker's email or a /submit/ row (writes nothing here)
npm run launch:draft -- --add <draft.json>                     add a reviewed draft to this file
npm run launch:check       the preflight: fields, links, images (sizes, formats, alt text), date, facts, listing
npm run seed:check         validate this file and print what would be loaded (changes nothing)
npm run seed:preview       load it, plus the samples, into the preview database
npm run seed:remote        load it into the live D1 database (founder's approval first; samples are refused there)
Maker images go in public/launches/<slug>/ and are referenced as /launches/<slug>/logo.png etc.
Re-running the seed updates entries in place and never touches votes. Use --prune to also remove launches deleted from this file.

launches.tagline: Practice interviews out loud. Know what to improve.
launches.description:
Abhyas is a free, open-source web app for practicing job interviews out loud. An AI interviewer reads your resume and the job description, asks questions matched to your experience level, and shows which skills to improve.

It is built for students and job seekers, with no account needed. Bring your own AI key, or run a local model for text interviews.

screenshots.alt: Abhyas home page: practice interviews with private AI
Abhyas live interview question with an answer box
Abhyas choosing an AI source: your own key or a local model
Abhyas profile setup: target role, experience level and resume
Abhyas session setup: interview type, style and length

launches.maker_story:
I'm Samyak, a 2026 CS grad, and I built Abhyas because good interview practice is hard to find: coaching costs money, and reading question lists doesn't teach you to answer out loud. It's an AI interviewer that reads your resume and the job description, adapts to your experience level, and shows which skills to work on.

I made it free and open source (MIT), with no accounts, and you bring your own AI key or run a local model, so I never see your resume or answers. I'd love your feedback on the questions and scoring: tell me what felt useful and what didn't.
